views.label: Keypress to write
views.note: Enter/a class hotkey triggers an optimistic queue removal before the API call resolves.

views.label: Failure rollback
views.note: A failed write restores the removed item at its original index and cursor — never a silently-vanished item.

views.label: Z undo round trip
views.note: Z replays the server-side undo endpoint, then re-inserts the item locally from the server's response.

cards.title: Removal happens before the network call resolves
items: removeFromQueue() drops the item and advances the cursor synchronously, returning a restore closure
Every caller (assign, discard) must invoke that closure on failure — mutation testing caught exactly this bug three times before extraction

cards.title: One undo, however many crops it touched
items: undoStore is a Z ring buffer shared by bulk label, move, discard, VLM-accept-all, and a dismiss — one press reverts the whole action, in the order it actually happened
Discard deliberately does NOT push an undoStore entry; it's reversible via a separate Dismissed panel, not Z

cards.title: Undo restores server state first, then the local queue
items: POST /crops/label/undo_batch is the source of truth for what got restored — the controller never guesses the pre-undo state
The cached reason (ReviewItem carries a served reason Crop doesn't) is reattached from a local map at removal time, not invented
